key_insight: T2D-Bench tests whether LLM answers for type 2 diabetes include explicit, graph-checkable evidence and guideline-consistent reasoning, not just fluent advice.
clinical_relevance: This matters because diabetes recommendations can sound correct while missing safety, lifestyle, or guideline evidence needed for trustworthy clinical use.
method: Built a multi-layer clinical-lifestyle knowledge graph linking UMLS, DrugBank, SIDER, ADA rules, and lifestyle-to-glycemia evidence.
Evaluated LLM outputs on 100 structured vignettes covering diagnosis, medication safety, and adversarial lifestyle conflicts.
Used an evidence gate plus constrained revision to detect unsupported claims and repair outputs toward verifier-level compliance.
evidence_signal: Across 100 vignettes, baseline outputs failed evidence-path checks in 35% of GPT-4o-mini cases and 33% of GPT-4o cases.
watch_item: Benchmark results depend on the completeness and correctness of the underlying knowledge graph, so gaps in encoded evidence could affect what is flagged as unsupported.
paper_title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
